Verdict: Caught.

Story: SEED-396#replace-evaluation-shell-checks, selected revision 004d9915bbc222a4404e69531fcf62e005720014. Source: .planning/seeds/SEED-396-evaluation-javascript-tests.md#replace-evaluation-shell-checks, Worked example; plan: .planning/slice-plans/679-evaluation-checks-state-facts-plainly/PLAN.md, slice 2. The source promises that rewritten checks keep every existing fact. Inspection validated the proposed narrow promise: native-run-timeout.sh must detect a new timed-out context attempt changing a previously completed retained attempt. Its unchanged fixture creates results/codex/context/clear/prior-complete, records completed/prior payload and events, and copies it to prior-copy.

Fault: In Distribution/evaluation/src/native-result-retain.sh, native_result_allocate_attempt, immediately after parent-directory creation at line 56, temporarily return the first existing attempt directory instead of allocating a new one. This models accidental reuse and overwrite of prior evidence. Fixtures and assertions remained byte-identical. Exact edit: /tmp/seed396-intent-coverage/fault.patch.

Maintained command in the isolated detached scratch, run unchanged for baseline, fault and restoration:
bash scripts/test.sh Distribution/evaluation/tests/native-harness/native-run-timeout.sh

Observation: Baseline exited 0; fault exited 1; restored run exited 0. The faulted runner explicitly stopped at native-run-timeout.sh:78, diff -rq "${prior}" "${prior_copy}" > /dev/null. Earlier timeout, cleanup, process and no-retry assertions passed before that line.

Independent wrong-behavior witness: A scratch PATH wrapper around diff copied both compared directories before their cleanup, read and hashed their record bytes, then returned the actual /usr/bin/diff status. The expected prior record contained "execution-status: completed" and "payload: prior"; the observed prior record had been overwritten with the new context/clear timeout record, including source-revision 004d9915bbc222a4404e69531fcf62e005720014. Expected record SHA-256 da3726c75c1e7c866bec097ddfd13fdc6b359077fbf1323c3bef4064210542f5; actual 44820d7b7797ef81d0b410e52f9dec4a9b270e2cd0973c9b91bbe7c80471d37e. The maintained directory comparison returned 1. Thus the maintained check reached the actual corrupted prior evidence and caught it, beyond merely executing the injected fault. The claim is limited to this retained-prior-attempt path.

Next proof action: No additional proof or assertion repair is indicated for this observed path. The caller can use this result for the configured wrap-up disposition. This single probe does not establish coverage of every story promise.

Prior disposition: This independently supports the existing keep-every-fact obligation. The plan's already accepted timeout retry and five other named breaks target different failures. This probe makes no new repair or backlog decision.

Restoration and setup: Created owned detached scratch /tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-396-prior-attempt-scratch at the selected revision and recorded its clean pre-probe state. Deterministic npm ci completed against the unchanged lockfile from the scratch working directory; an earlier --prefix invocation was rejected before installation and was corrected without modifying the lockfile. A finally block restored exact original production bytes, checked unchanged fixture/assertion bytes and equality with pre-probe Git status, and reran the same command successfully. The independent restored witness also saw identical prior bytes. Final status remained clean. Removed the owned scratch and verified its filesystem and Git worktree-list absence. No branch was created, no stash was used, and the execution checkout was not modified.

Evidence retained outside the retired scratch: /tmp/seed396-intent-coverage/probe-transcript.txt; runs.json; baseline-times.tsv, fault-times.tsv and restored-times.tsv; corresponding outcomes and logs; wrong-behavior.json; fault/observed-prior and fault/expected-prior; fault/record.diff; fault/assertion-status.txt; restoration.txt; scratch-retirement.txt; npm-ci-cwd.log.
